items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

items.title: Ngành Công nghệ thông tin có những đặc điểm nào?
items.summary:
Ngành Công nghệ thông tin (CNTT) là lĩnh vực nghiên cứu có tính liên ngành cao, kết hợp giữa toán học, điện tử – viễn thông, khoa học máy tính và quản trị để thiết kế, xy dựng, vận hành, giám sát và tối ưu các hệ thống xử lý thông tin trên nền tảng máy tính và mạng. Trọng tm của CNTT không chỉ nằm ở việc viết mã nguồn, mà ở khả năng tổ chức dòng chảy thông tin trong một tổ chức: từ khu thu thập, chuẩn hóa, lưu trữ, truyền dẫn, xử lý, phn tích cho đến khai thác thông tin phục vụ ra quyết định và [...] Mặc dù thường được nhắc chung, Công nghệ thông tin, Khoa học máy tính, Kỹ thuật phần mềm và Kỹ thuật máy tính là những ngành có trọng tm, triết lý đào tạo và định hướng nghề nghiệp khác nhau, dù có nhiều học phần giao thoa.

Công nghệ thông tin tập trung vào việc ứng dụng công nghệ để giải quyết bài toán thực tế trong tổ chức. Chương trình thường nhấn mạnh: [...] Về chuyên môn, CNTT bao gồm nhiều trụ cột như phát triển phần mềm, dữ liệu, mạng máy tính, hệ thống, điện toán đám my, trí tuệ nhn tạo và an toàn thông tin. Sinh viên thường học từ nền tảng Toán, thuật toán, cấu trúc dữ liệu, lập trình, cơ sở dữ liệu, hệ điều hành, mạng, bảo mật đến các học phần ứng dụng như web, mobile, AI, Big Data, DevOps, IoT, hệ thống thông tin và chuyển đổi số. Chương trình học thường kết hợp lý thuyết với thực hành, đồ án, dự án nhóm, thực tập và portfolio cá nhn.

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.

items.title: Pulkit Agrawal (Eka Robotics): Why Robots Need Practice to Master the Physical World | Physical AI
items.summary:
MIT associate professor and Eka Robotics cofounder Pulkit Agrawal explains the difference between planning a task and physically executing it. He argues that broader skills must be matched by speed, precision and reliability before robots become products people want to use. [...] Through demonstrations of delicate object handling, including a raspberry, he presents Eka’s approach to physical control and reports a picking rate of 1,500 objects per hour. He then explains reinforcement learning, or learning through trial and error, and how the demonstrated manipulation systems were trained entirely in simulation before their skills were transferred to physical robots. items.title: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation | NVIDIA Blog
items.summary:
The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems.

At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models, simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. [...] A simulated tool-sorting task demonstrates how VABAR evaluates robot manipulation skills for industrial workflows.

## Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs

Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge.

Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge. [...] “To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects.

Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation.

Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios.

Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL.
